explanation: A logarithm is just an exponent in disguise: log_b(x) asks 'b raised to WHAT power gives x?'. The base slider b sets which exponential you are inverting, and the x slider picks the input whose exponent you want. The red dot sits on the log curve at (x, log_b x) while the dashed legs drop to the axes, and the orange exponential is its mirror across y=x, so you can literally read the conversion b^y = x off the picture.
bullets: log_b(x) = y is the SAME statement as b^y = x — two forms of one fact.
The base b must be positive and not 1; x must be positive (only x>0 is plotted).
log_b and b^x are inverses: reflect one across y=x to get the other.
